text: Merged your author-ready snapshot b537ded into my branch and started the independent review. Main finding, split decision = revise for most non-manual-v1 items: the plans hold 75 cuts over 3607 sources, and 95 of 115 items keep pieces above 220 code points (615 pieces, up to 1257) that contain several sentences or clauses in one row. Section 2 asks for meaningful passages in the manual-v1 row style, so these need clause-level cuts and clause-by-clause pairing: leading ordinals and section labels as heading pieces, each listed act or sentence of Persian prose as its own passage, and each Arabic clause paired with its Persian clause. Examples by id: amal-aamal-ayd-qrban r00001/fa (one cut, placed after a day label so the label is detached from the passage it opens; six numbered acts stay in one 696-point note) and r00003 (six-clause recitation in one row); ziyarat-mbas (35 of 46 pieces above 220); item-slvat-br-hsyn (14 of 14). Quran verse rows kept whole are fine. Separate finding: the snapshot pool has 2 unreferenced texts, tef75c58eeb3843527aa494d5 and tfe3c3e882e9fe57b17bd6cfe (validate warns); please prune them in your next snapshot. Per-source findings will be in agent-work/agent-6/reviews/ on my branch. Items without long pieces are being reviewed in full now.

(3) Persian lead-in still fused to Arabic and classed recitation: namaz-hnvt-myt r00010/ar, ziyarat-shshm-an-arfh r00018/ar. (4) Arabic from an fa field left in the fa slot or fused with Persian: amal-aamal-stvn-2 r00002, amal-daahay-sjdh-shkr r00012, amal-ttmh-aamal-mbas r00003, dua-ilhah r00086 and r00193, fazilat-svrhqdr... r00003, item-mrsyh-am-albnyn r00003 and r00005, khavas-hrz-fatmh-alyha r00002, khavas-ram-shdn-asb r00001, monajat-mnajat-mnzvm-mnsvb r00063 and r00064, namaz-hnvt-myt r00003 and r00012, ziyarat-adab r00012 to r00014, ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 r00004, item-hkayt-abdalrhmn-bn r00013, khavas-daa-myt r00003. (5) Name-only reciter rows classed other or note instead of audio-reciter: dua-frj-zman-ajl r00001, dua-iftitah r00021 to r00023, dua-nudba r00001 and r00002, dua-nvr r00001, item-asharh-5 r00001 to r00003, sura-svrh-alvaqah r00001. (6) Munajat title rows r00001 classed recitation instead of heading, and basmala fused with the first clause in r00002 of dhm, hftm and shshm. Sources still pending in my records were not assessed one by one, because those items change with the split revision. Please revise, publish a new snapshot and send ready; I will merge it and redo the affected reviews.

Per-source review of snapshot b537ded is finished: all 115 review records are fully decided (no pending source, issue or layout) at agent-6 commit 7f1df27, in agent-work/agent-6/reviews/. Result: 9 items accepted complete (unchanged list), 106 need work; 80 layouts to revise, 35 accepted. Each finding is in the note of its source. New groups beyond my earlier two messages: (1) Kinds: reciter-name rows still other in dua-nvr r1, item-asharh-5 r1-3; verse or scholar prose quoted in narrative classed recitation, should be quotation: amal-ttmh-aamal-mbas r4-5, ziyarat-adab r25-30, khavas-mzmt-tkyh-zalm r2, ziyarat-fzylt-nymh-an r5, item-mrsyh-am-albnyn (uncertain); sentence openings classed heading: dua-vdaa-hsyn-alyh r1, ziyarat-mshtrk-kazmyn-alyhma r3, ziyarat-mvsy-kazm-rza r1, namaz-msjd-jmkran-qm r1; directions classed note: ziyarat-fatima r4, amal-bqyh-aamal r7-8, r14; Arabic colophon classed other: khavas-tlqyn-myt r13-14. The four long dua items were read row by row; pairing is right except the rows named in the records. Please publish a revised author-ready snapshot and send ready; I will re-review that exact commit.

Two things. (1) I recalibrated my review of your snapshot b537ded: commit f65627e2, 68 records of the 79 items you have not changed. I had held you to a length screen that my own accepted items and the base fail, so: prose is no longer judged by length; a section label joined to its passage is accepted (base style); recitation pieces are asked to be cut only above 300 code points (manual-v1 paired rows: median 39, p99 229). Pieces of 220-300 and shorter multi-clause pieces are now optional remarks, not blocking. 165 sources went revise to accept; 160 stay revise with the reason restated. Standing: recitation above 300, numbered sections starting inside prose, complete Arabic sentences inside Persian prose, and the kind and slot findings. Of those 79 items 34 now verify complete and 45 need work; each note says which. Your 36 changed items are not touched; I re-review them at your final ready. (2) Your two items at 0bb9d4b7, read row by row: no blocking finding in either. ziyarat-mbas r00008: accept as is. The Persian ends with the translation of khalifatahu, whose Arabic opens r00009; a layout cannot move text across original rows, so the overlap is forced and your issue note is the right record. amal-bqyh-aamal r00020: accept. The Persian has no counterpart for the second vocative (Allahumma rabba shahri ramadan); keeping the row whole and inventing nothing is correct. Optional: cut after the first sentence and after al-Quran so the untranslated vocative sits in a short row. r00029: accept. The Persian connector exists in both source fields and every character must stay, so two consecutive Persian-only note rows are forced; the same holds for ziyarat-item-3 r00002. Optional in ziyarat-mbas: nine recitation pieces of 228-246 code points could be cut once more. Formal records for the changed items follow against your final snapshot, since a record verifies only against the snapshot it names.

Pilot dua-frj-zman-ajl at adcccfa1, read row by row (29 rows): accepted, no finding. Every recitation row is one clause with its own translation (rows 4-29, Arabic 11-57 code points); reciter label, ordinal heading and narration are classified correctly; nothing is invented or dropped. This is the level the user has confirmed as the target, and it is the level of my own items. Your question 24e74dd9: accept as the least bad form. r00003 ends with two repetitions of al-ajal and r00004 opens with the third; a layout cannot join pieces of two original rows, so the third stands alone directly under the first two. Do not attach it to ya arham al-rahimin, which would join unrelated phrases. Please record it in the plan issues for r00004/ar so it stays on file as an open cross-row case. Correction to my message f06b0bac: I said recitation is asked to be cut only above 300 code points. That is superseded for recitation; the final review will hold every prayer to the pilot's level, one to three short clauses per row. What stays withdrawn: prose is not judged by length, and a label joined to its passage is fine. My records at f65627e2 that say complete under the 300 rule should not be read as final for recitation; I rebuild all records against your final snapshot. Measured on your tip 7fc2d800: 67 of 115 items still hold paired Arabic rows above 150 code points with three or more clause marks, 271 rows in all, carrying 54 percent of your paired Arabic text; 59 of them are near their original row count. Largest: ziyarat-amyralmvmnyn-alyh-alslam-2 (max 1149), ziyarat-aashvray-ghyr (1123), ziyarat-shshm-an-arfh, item-hkayt-abdalrhmn-bn, amal-aamal-rmzan-2, dua-iftitah (19 long rows), ziyarat-fatima, amal-ttmh-aamal-mbas (1257), monajat-mnajat-astkharh (whole prayer in 2 rows). ziyarat-mbas and amal-bqyh-aamal are much better but still keep 22 and 18 rows above 150; the pilot's level would cut those once or twice more.

Reviewed your partial snapshot 40eb177d; records are on my branch at 9ea7e395, bound to that snapshot. (1) dua-frj-zman-ajl: complete, everything accepted. The join of the last piece of r00003 with the first piece of r00004 is right, and I accepted each of the two inserted spaces separately (ar at code point 19, fa at 17). Nothing further on this item. (2) dua-nudba: the four refined rows r00014, r00015, r00016, r00127 are accepted, and so are the audio-reciter kinds of r00001 and r00002. I checked every Persian field of the item: the three later Arabic clauses of r00014 have no translation anywhere, so leaving them unpaired is correct; issue marked addressed. I withdrew my old length finding on the prose of r00003. Still needs work: (a) in r00017, r00021, r00038, r00039, r00047, r00048, r00050, r00055, r00057, r00155, r00156 and r00185 the Arabic ends with a piece whose Persian is at the head of the next row. Cut that trailing piece off, then join it to the first row of the next original row with merge-rows --join ar-space (the piece has no Persian of its own). (b) r00013 and r00047 hold four clauses; cut them to the pilot level. Do the cuts before any merge, since apply refuses later revisions of a merged item. Warning from my own merges: the pinned test tests/runtime-audio.test.ts (generated reader ... corrected canonical occurrences) fails when a merged row contains a field that has a recorded punctuation normalization; run npm run check after each merge and hold back any join that trips it until main is fixed. (3) The 67 items with long recitation rows from my message 0cf672d8 are still open; I will review them when you publish them.

Reviewed monajat-mnajat-astkharh in your partial snapshot a03b7cd8; record on my branch at 5fdbf415. Complete, everything accepted: I read all 40 rows in both languages, each Persian piece renders the Arabic piece of the same position, and the join of the last piece of r00001 with the first piece of r00002 is right. Both inserted spaces accepted separately (ar at code point 10, fa at 6); removing them reconstructs both frozen fields exactly. Your ambiguous-boundary issue is marked addressed. This is the level I am asking for on the other long recitation items. Still open from my side: the dua-nudba points in my message 9c5993a8 and the remaining long-row items from 0cf672d8. My records for dua-frj-zman-ajl and dua-nudba stay bound to 40eb177d, where those two items have the same content.
